title: st list defaults to in-progress only and its output discloses the filter nowhere
body:
`intent st list` with no flags renders only in-progress threads, and nothing in the OUTPUT says so -- the filter is disclosed solely in `--help` ("default: in progress only"). A filtered view with no filter disclosure is indistinguishable from missing data, and it was reported as exactly that: the tool's own author read the four-row output against thirteen thread directories on disk and a 67-thread store, and filed it as a bug.

## The measurement that reconciles the three surfaces (2026-08-28)

    intent st list                    -> 6 rows (the WIP set at that moment)
    intent st list --status all       -> 67 threads
    status histogram                  -> 52 Completed, 2 Cancelled, 6 WIP, 5 Triage, 1 NotStarted, 1 OnHold
    grep -c '^STEELTHREAD:' intent/.intentfiles -> 13
    thread dirs under intent/st/      -> 13

67 - 52 - 2 = 13: the realised set is exactly every non-terminal thread, `.intentfiles` and the disk agree entry-for-entry, and the bare listing is exactly the WIP subset. **Nothing is inconsistent. The defect is that the bare output carries no way to know that.**

## The class

Same family as No Silent Errors applied to a read surface: a default that narrows the answer must SAY it narrowed the answer, or every comparison against another surface (disk, views, the store) reads as corruption. The operator cost is real -- the report this issue is filed from cost the author a cross-surface investigation that one output line would have prevented.

## Remedy directions (for ruling, not chosen here)

1. A disclosure footer on every filtered render: `6 of 67 threads (in progress) -- use --status all for the full list`. Cheapest; keeps the default.
2. Change the default to `--status all` and let the terminal renderer's width handling carry the size. Honest but noisy for the common case.
3. Both surfaces stay, plus the same footer on `st list --status <x>` (any narrowed render), so the rule is "a narrowed answer names its scope", not a special case for the default.

Direction 3 is the general form of the rule; 1 is its minimum.
